newsitem.title: USA: Tropical Storm Lili stalls, slowly strengthens.
newsitem.headline: Tropical Storm Lili stalls, slowly strengthens.

text.p: Tropical Storm Lili stalled temporarily south-southwest of Cuba Wednesday, but was expected to resume a northward drift, the National Hurricane Center said.
At 1400 EDT/1800 GMT, Lili's center was near latitude 18.3 north and longitude 84.5 west, or about 365 miles (585 km) south-southwest of Havana.
Maximum sustained winds had increased to near 65 mph (100 kph) in a small area near its center and some strengthening was likely during the next 24 hours.
Forecasters also warned that rainfall of 12 inches (30 cm) and higher was possible over parts of Cuba and Central America.
"Data from hurricane hunters indicate that Lili has temporarily stalled," the National Hurricane Center said. "In a few hours, Lili is expected to resume a northward drift."
Forecasters said they expected a turn toward the north-northeast during the next 24 hours, but said Lili's slower movement meant a hurricane watch was not yet necessary for the Florida Keys.

As of 1400/1800, a hurricane watch and tropical storm warning were in effect for the Isle of Youth and the western mainland provinces of Pinar Del Rio, Havana, Matanzas, Villa Clara and Cienfuegos in Cuba and a tropical storm warning was in effect for the east coast of Mexico's Yucatan Peninsula from Cabo Catoche south to Bahia de Chetumal and for the Cayman Islands.
